title: OIG Report: ICE Electronic Health Record System Fails to Transfer Medical Records, Risking Patient Harm
excerpt: A DHS Office of Inspector General audit (OIG-26-18) found that ICE's electronic health record system cannot interface with external data sources, lacks a patient portal for detainees, and creates risk of "untimely and inaccurate" medical decisions that could result in patient harm and wasted taxpayer funds.
content:
On July 23, 2026, the DHS Office of Inspector General released audit report OIG-26-18, finding that ICE's electronic health record (eHR) system does not meet basic capability needs for the ICE Health Services Corps (IHSC), which provides medical care to detained immigrants.

The OIG found the eHR system failed to interface with external data sources and access outside medical information, did not include a patient portal allowing detained individuals to access their records after leaving custody, and lacked key functionality needed for continuity of care — all increasing the risk of untimely and inaccurate healthcare decisions that could result in patient harm.

  • The report warned of potential waste of taxpayer funds due to system deficiencies.
  • The audit was conducted against a backdrop of record ICE detainee deaths in 2026, with 26 reported deaths by September 1, 2026 — on pace to exceed the 2025 record of 33.
  • ICE concurred with the OIG's recommendations, which were left open and resolved pending implementation.
  • The OIG noted that three government shutdowns in FY2026 significantly delayed the audit's publication.
